newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JAN 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JAN 13.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The worst flash flooding in the last 40 years vents its fury in Corinth with three dead and four missing. In Corinth the Xyropotamos broke its banks and turned streets into raging rivers sweeping car and trucks in its wake.
-- Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos sees light at the end of the tunnel for the current Yugoslav crisis, following his talks with Slobodan Milosevic and opposition leaders in Belgrade.
--A new nationwide survey of youth shows that their main priorities are to make a better society and to find jobs that are challenging and satisfying.
--Residents of the areas worst hit by the floods - Corinth, Fthiotida and Argolida - condemn the authorities for negligence after the worst storms in 50 years.
--Six dead and three missing is the toll according to Eleftheros Typos. The government was caught off guard by the fury of the storms. Eight cities now under water.
--US State Department official Carey Kavanaugh arrives in Cyprus to recommend the freezing of the purchase of Russian-made S-300 missiles and the implementation of a moratorium on flyovers.
--Dramatic moments for the 25 passengers of the bus swept away by raging torrents.

--Italian papers reveal that the 283 illegal immigrants alleged to have drowned in the ramming of a boat int he Mediterranean Sea were locked into the fridge of a small fishing boat. Britain's 'Observer' criticises the indifference afforded to the disappearance of 283 people. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
